recipes.name: Slow Cooker London Broil
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Place meat in the bottom of the slow cooker; if necessary, slice meat to make it fit.
In a medium bowl, mix together mushroom and tomato soup. Pour mixture over beef. Sprinkle dry onion soup mix over top.
Cover, and cook on Low for 8 to 10 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker London Broil
raw_recipe.description: This crockpot London Broil is easy and tasty. The steak is flavored with condensed soup, with dry onion soup mix added on top — together in the slow cooker for a one-pot meal.

review.reviewBody:
My family loved this. I love the rich flavor the tomato soup adds. Here's what I did the second time to make it perfect:
-Used London Broil, not flank steak.
-Add 1 tbl worcestershire
-Add 1 tbl red wine vinegar
-Mix all 3 soups together first.
-Added some carrots and potatoes - To keep them from changing the flavor of the sauce and soaking most of it up, I place the veggies in some aluminum foil, fold the sides up to make a little boat and sit on top of the meat - I read this trick in a cooking magazine.

I did the recipe as suggested (Mostly) I doubled the soup and added the wine and Worcestershire, the flavor was great!

I must stress that there is a difference between slow cookers. Mine is relatively new at two years old, so the "low" setting is not the same as a cooker that is 5 or more years old.

I put in both flank steak and stew meat. 10 hours turned the flank steak in to a stringy hairball (still tasted good, just visually icky) but the stew meat turned out nicely.

So, if you have a newer cooker, make the necessary time adjustment, or use Stew/Top Round. 

I will definitely make this again

I made this recipe with a few changes. I used the condensed tomato soup but instead of cream of mushroom, I used 98% fat free cream of celery. I added a few dashes of whostishire and instead of using onion soup mix, which is loaded with salt, I substituted fat free, sodium free beef bullion and dried onion. I mixed it all together and before pouring it over the meat, I pierced the meat several times with a fork being careful NOT to go all the way through meat. I also took the time to caramelize some onion and served it with those...boy did that just put it over the top! Being a year post bariatric surgery, I'm always looking for recipes I can alter to fit my diet and this one is definitely a keeper!

I changed a few minor things. First, I used London Broil, not flank steaks. I only used half a package of a Knorr's onion soup mix. I sprinkled a little bit over the meat before pouring the sauce and added a little bit more on top of the sauce. I also cooked it on high for the first four hours then on low for another two hours. I found it was all I needed for a pound and a half of meat. Everyone enjoyed it at my dinner party. I will definitely make it again!

Good. And I made lots of changes. First, this is not London Broil, it's slow cooker flank steak. That's OK, the base of this recipe is a good place to start for slow cooker meat recipes. I doubled the soups because I saw another reviewer do it for more gravy. Then I used two London broil steaks; weighing a little over a pound each. I added a box of fresh mushrooms (cut in half). I added a large cut up onion. Added a tablespoon of pepper, a splash of worchester and white wine.
It tasted good. The family ate it and thought it was alright. It's a little salty so definitely should be served with a starch. We had it with rice but mashed potatoes would be even better. I'm gonna keep this as one of my base plans for when I have a tough meat and don't want a lot of work. Thanks for inspiring my recipe.

I had to try this based on simplicity, and the twist with tomato soup! 2 minor changes: Fresh onion layered on bottom ( omit dry mix), I always marinade the meat before cooking in crock pot (simple mix of olive oil, steak sauce, lemon juice, Worcester sauce). Follow as directed. Cooking for dinner that night 
, cook on high for 5 to 6 hours. (I had a 1lb London broil). Served with mashed potatoes and fresh veggies. Plenty of sauce to do with egg noodles or over rice.
Had the family begging for more! ENJOY!

i used a 3# chuck roast instead of flank steak or london broil & browned it in oil first, then, As someone else did, i added 1 TBS each of worcestshire sauce & red wine vinegar to the soups. Added 1" slices of carrots & 5 small new potatoes, halved, some fresh mushrooms & cooked on Low for 6-7 hours. YUM!

This sounded like a recipe my husband would love. After reading the reviews, I took a few tips I felt would work for me. I mixed the soups together and added Worcester sauce before pouring over the meat. Half of the dry soup mix was enough. Used top round for meat and seasoned with Montreal seasoning. Was even better warmed up a few days later!

I really took liberties with this recipe based on what I had on hand, and it came out great (for the most part). My husband brought home two different London broil top round steaks, both came out different, one being tougher than the other even though they were cooked exactly the same. So those of you saying your steak was tough...it wasn't the recipe, it's the steak. Since we had 4 lbs of steak I needed to double the recipe. For one reason or another, either not having a specific item or having decided through a review to make a change, I ended up using: 1 can tomato soup, 1/2 can tomato paste, 1 can cream of celery soup, 1 can beef gravy, 1 small can mushroom pieces (including liquid), 1/4 c. onion flakes, 3 T Worcestershire, 1/4 c. red wine vinegar. Mixed together and let steak marinate overnight. Tossed into crock pot and cooked on low for almost 9 hours. One steak, the thicker of the two, fell apart like pot roast. The other steak was tougher, but still tasty. Served with Practically Perfect Basmati Rice, and there was plenty of sauce to top the rice with. Thanks Merri C. for a tasty and very forgiving recipe.
We loved this. I switched the Campbell's cream of mushroom soup with Campbell's cream of onion soup and I also added carrots to it.....I will definitely be making this again!

I made this last night and will certainly make again. I only had a 1.25lb London Broil so used 1 can of tomato soup and 1 can of chicken soup. I added chopped onion, celery, carrotts and green bell pepper on the bottom of the slow cooker and put the meat on the top. For the sauce I mixed the two soups together and then added a couple of tablespoons of red wine, a dash of worcestershire sauce and some minced garlic plus a little water. The result was wonderful and smelt amazing when I got home. Served over tagliatelle pasta and it was wonderful. Thanks for a great receipe.

This dish is well worth the costs in both money and time. It turned out delicious and the meat melts in your mouth. The first change I made to it was adding diced Portabella mushrooms. Secondly, I didn't have any condensed tomato soup so I added a reconstituted package I had laying around. So in my version, there was less tang to the taste.
So easy and so delicious
Use onions instead of dry onion soup mix to decrease salt.
Quick preparation and tastes great.
My husband didn't like it and only ate it after putting BBQ sauce in it. Maybe if I had used half can of tomato soup instead of a whole can that might have been better.
Wonderful sauce and fall apart meat. I will add some water to the sauce next time so there will be enough to go over potatoes and drizzle over the meat. Delicious.
This was delicious. I would not make any changes. I will make it again.
I limed the tenderness of the meat, but I didn't jump up and down over the "gravy" like I thought I would. I will try another gravy the next time.

Made this for dinner last night and loved it!! I had to use a top round roast because I couldn’t find flank steak. I was also going to add two cans of each mushroom soup and tomato, but I’m glad I didn’t because we had enough sauce for our mashed potatoes! It’s just two of us, so if we would have had others I would probably add more. This was a big hit! Thanks for sharing!
